extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and other attorneys who practice before the USPTO; counsel and respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order describing alleged violations of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, the legal conclusions, mitigating factors, and the sanctions/probation/monitoring requirements imposed on a registered practitioner. It sets procedural and substantive obligations for practitioners and the Office in disciplinary settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — dishonesty/fraud/deceit/misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the Final Order: filing checks with the Office drawn on the practitioner's operating bank account and failing to maintain sufficient funds when the checks were presented for collection constitutes conduct involving dishonesty/deceit under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in conduct reflecting adversely on a practitioner's fitness to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order treats the submission of dishonored checks and related failures as conduct that reflects adversely on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(b) — commingling/unearned client funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes commingling funds belonging to the practitioner or the practitioner's firm with advanced funds belonging to a client (i.e., failing to deposit unearned client funds in a sequestered/trust account).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulated facts: respondent did not deposit funds received from clients in a fiduciary account and represented that some dishonored checks did not represent fiduciary funds. The Order treats the failure to maintain client funds in trust accounts and commingling of personal/business funds with client funds as a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — neglect of entrusted legal matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes neglect of an entrusted legal matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where respondent failed to timely pay fees to the Office for which the client had advanced funds (or otherwise relied on the practitioner to pay), causing delays/abandonments of applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain sufficient funds / avoid submitting dishonored checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must ensure funds are sufficient when submitting checks to the USPTO for required fees (or otherwise ensure payment via deposit account instructions), to avoid dishonored checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences shown: dishonored checks led to Notices of Abandonment or Notices to File Missing Parts, required payment of additional surcharges, petitions to revive, and delays in examination/filing. The RCE or filing forms should include instructions if payment is to be taken from a deposit account rather than by check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper handling of client retainer/advanced funds (fiduciary duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds received from clients that are advanced for costs/filing fees must be treated properly (i.e., placed in appropriate trust/fiduciary accounts until fees are earned or properly applied).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulated practice: respondent advanced fees on behalf of clients and then billed them; failing to segregate such funds resulted in commingling findings. The Order emphasizes that funds represented as client advances are subject to fiduciary handling requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely communication to clients and obligations to notify clients of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must inform affected clients of relevant disciplinary events and comply with notification requirements imposed by the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific obligations: provide, within 30 days of the Final Order, a copy of the Final Order to Clients I–V and file, within 45 days of the Final Order, an affidavit with the OED Director stating compliance with that requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors that may affect discipline severity
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances that may mitigate discipline include remediation actions, payment of outstanding fees/surcharges, cessation of the misconduct, and lack of prior disciplinary history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the Order: respondent paid the application and returned-check processing fees, had not submitted insufficient-fund checks since a stated date, and had no prior disciplinary record; no client reported substantial harm. These factors were cited as mitigation in deciding the stayed suspension/probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions structure: stayed suspension and probation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose suspension but stay its execution conditioned on successful completion of a probationary period with detailed terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case: a 24-month suspension was imposed but fully stayed so long as respondent served and successfully completed a 24-month probation with conditions (e.g., not committing further misconduct, complying with the Final Order). During probation the respondent was permitted to practice before the Office unless the stay is lifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice monitor requirement and monitoring/reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must hire (at own expense) a law office practice monitor acceptable to the OED Director to review practice and submit periodic reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor must prepare reports at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months addressing compliance with the USPTO Code regarding: (a) maintaining client funds in trust accounts, (b) managing law practice trust and operating accounts, and (c) maintaining and utilizing electronic and manual calendaring systems to assist in timely legal services. If not in compliance, the report must identify each disciplinary rule implicated and briefly explain the noncompliance. If a monitor cannot continue, respondent must promptly propose replacements for OED approval; failure to maintain an acceptable monitor may trigger a Show Cause order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show Cause / lifting the stay / immediate suspension process
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or any disciplinary rule during probation, OED issues an Order to Show Cause and may request the USPTO Director to lift the stay and suspend the respondent immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: OED sends Order to Show Cause to respondent's address of record, grants 15 days to respond; after considering response, OED may deliver the file to the USPTO Director and request lifting the stay and imposition of up to a 24-month suspension. If suspension is imposed, respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and OED will disseminate information per § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences upon suspension: dissemination and dissociation of PTO credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: When suspension occurs, the Office will disseminate the discipline and dissociate respondent's name from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates; respondent may not use or obtain customer numbers/PKI unless reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies immediate dissociation of customer numbers and PKI certificates and prohibition on use or acquisition of such credentials until reinstatement. OED dissemination per § 11.59 is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations for disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders and notices of discipline are to be published and notices given to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts where respondent is admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific actions: publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room electronically; publish a Notice of Stayed Suspension in the Official Gazette; pursuant to § 11.59, give notice of the public discipline and reasons to state disciplinary agencies, courts where respondent is admitted, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement procedural requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement resolving a disciplinary complaint must satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 to be approved by the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the Proposed Settlement Agreement satisfied § 11.26 and that the Director has authority under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26 to approve the agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office's reservation of right to seek further discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may seek additional discipline under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57 for misconduct not specifically addressed or for future related misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly states nothing in the Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline for any misconduct not addressed therein, and that the record (including this Final Order) may be considered in future proceedings as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations.
